claims.text: THE PUBLIC-INTEREST TEST IS GONE, AND THIS WAS CHECKED FROM BOTH SIDES. The phrase 'public interest' occurs zero times in EO 12356, as does any form of 'balanc'. Its predecessor EO 12065 had required at section 3-303 that an official 'determine whether the public interest in disclosure outweighs the damage to national security'. The obligation to weigh disclosure against harm was removed in 1982 and has not returned.

RECLASSIFICATION AFTER DISCLOSURE IS EXPRESSLY AUTHORISED. Section 1.6(c) permits officials to 'reclassify information previously declassified and disclosed if it is determined in writing' that it requires protection and 'may reasonably be recovered'. Section 1.6(d) permits classification or reclassification AFTER an agency has received a request under the Freedom of Information Act, the Privacy Act or the mandatory review provisions, on a document-by-document basis.
Section 1.1(c) resolves doubt toward secrecy: where there is reasonable doubt about the level, the information is to be safeguarded at the higher level.

IT DID NOT REVOKE EO 11652, and the claim that it did is wrong. EO 12065 had already revoked 11652 in 1978. Also note that the Federation of American Scientists URL usually given for this order, irp.fas.org/offdocs/eo/eo-12356.htm, returns HTTP 404 and does not exist.

timeline.text: Reagan's classification order, effective 1 August 1982, revokes EO 12065. The phrase 'public interest' occurs nowhere in it. Section 1.6(c) permits reclassifying information already declassified and disclosed where it may reasonably be recovered, and 1.6(d) permits classification or reclassification after a Freedom of Information Act request has been received. Doubt about the level is resolved upward.
